sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example is written more briefly. Fill in the reasoning it leaves out.

items.prompt: Six boxes hold 8 markers each, and 3 markers are loose. Which expression represents the total?

steps: Six equal groups of 8 are represented by 6 × 8.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A library has 17 shelves with 27 books on each shelf. Then 17 books are loaned out. How many books remain?
In 8188768, how does the value of the 8 in the thousands place compare with the value of the 8 in the ten-thousands place?
choices: 1/10 as much
100 times as much
the same value
10 times as much

items.prompt: Round each number to the nearest thousand to estimate 557500 + 328500.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Round 992 to the nearest hundred and 22 to the nearest ten, then multiply to estimate the product.
A student says 3454 - 3385 = 169. Round each number to the nearest hundred. Which choice correctly checks the claim?
choices: The claim is exact; the rounded estimate is 100.
The claim is not exact; the exact result is 69 and the rounded estimate is 100.
The claim is exact; the rounded estimate is 200.
The claim is not exact; the exact result is 69 and the rounded estimate is 200.

items.prompt: A student evaluates 6 × [21 + (10 - 5)] + 23: “They multiply 6 by 21 first, then finish the calculation, so the value is 154.” Which statement best identifies the error?
choices: The student used the right first step but made an arithmetic slip; the value should be 181.
The grouping symbols do not affect the order; 154 is the value.
The work is correct; 154 is the value.
The student multiplied before evaluating (10 - 5); the innermost difference is 5, giving 179.

items.prompt: A student says, “In 2639999, the value of the 9 in the tens place is 100 times as much as the value of the 9 in the hundreds place.” Which statement best analyzes the error?
choices: The places are adjacent, so 90 is 100 times as much as 900.
The values are 90 and 900; 90 is 100 times as much as 900, so the student's comparison is correct.
Both digits have value 9; repeated digits always have the same value.
The values are 90 and 900; 90 is 1/10 as much as 900, so the student's comparison is incorrect.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: Which expression means: “Subtract 3 from 7, multiply the difference by 4, then add 69.”
Which phrase describes 65 + [8 × (25 - 12)] without evaluating it?
choices: Add 25 and 12, multiply the sum by 8, then add 65.
Subtract 12 from 25, multiply the difference by 8, then add 65.
Subtract 12 from 25, add 8, then multiply the sum by 65.
Multiply 8 by 25, add 65, then subtract 12.
